correctness.rationale: Exactness gives sum_j e_j=N. Set preservation contributes at least k/alpha from the k rejected ranks, while the remaining N-k entries are each at least the minimum m. Hence m<=(N-k/alpha)/(N-k). The two-level grid vector attains equality and the equality conditions make it unique. The lattice case alpha N integer forces all remaining mass to zero.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact quantitative limit on the practical reason for demanding positivity: avoiding catastrophic multiplicative collapse. It shows that exact set preservation permits positive values off the lattice but still forces the best possible worst-rank reserve to decay at most as O(1/N), and it gives the unique extremal grid pattern. This is a meaningful finite-sample benchmark rather than a routine restatement of validity.
